**Keep boundary failure state run-scoped.**

`observe_module_read` sets the process-wide `FAILED` flag for resolution or guard-lock failures. `Custody` retains its `Boundary` through `verify()`, but dropping it only decrements `ACTIVE`. A later `Custody` in the same process can therefore fail `self.boundary.verify()` after the earlier run has ended.

Do not only clear `FAILED` when `ACTIVE` reaches zero. Concurrent boundary registration can race with that reset. Store failure state per `State`, or synchronize registration, reset, and verification as one lifecycle.

**Canonicalize observed file paths before the boundary comparison.**

`Boundary::new` stores the canonical selected root, but `observe_module_read` compares it with `std::path::absolute(file)`, which preserves symlink components. A selected root symlink can therefore make an ordinary in-root read fail `strip_prefix`, set `escaped`, and reject the output-dir run.

The reverse case is also unsafe. An in-root symlink to an outside module passes the lexical comparison, while `std::fs::read(file)` follows the symlink and reads outside the selected root. Compare a canonicalized file path with the canonical root. For absent probes, canonicalize the deepest existing ancestor and append the remaining components. Reuse the canonical root from `Boundary::new` instead of canonicalizing the root for every read.

[P1] Preserve excluded lexical paths before resolving file aliases

Failure mode: the repaired canonicalization erases `.git` or Cargo-owned `target` from an observed path when a symlink there points back into captured source. The exclusion check now sees only the ordinary target path. Real exact-head CLI cases with `src/lib.rs = include!("../.git/linked.rs");` (and the analogous target path), where the link points to regular captured `src/impl.rs`, exit0 and publish both admission flags true, with two native findings. The retained original native binary refuses both; an exact pre-repair 0ffd boundary-module control also refuses the .git observation.

Why here: inventory deliberately skips these directories, including the alias bindings; docs/OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md promises the read/probe owner refuses such excluded paths. The target contents being captured does not bind the traversed alias inside a skipped directory. This is an exclusion/refusal regression, not an asserted outside-root escape or hostile-filesystem guarantee.

Fix direction: check selected-root-relative lexical exclusions as well as canonical containment/identity, reconciling requested/canonical root spellings so the selected-root-alias positive remains fixed. Preserve absent-probe and nonregular-input behavior.

Validation: add real CLI negatives for .git/target links to otherwise captured regular source, keeping the root-alias positive. [Raw fixtures, old/new native streams/manifests and audit](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/tree/fefe01683ed9974ad36f1a4f137abdefc4b6784c/repair490). Current native member lengths/hashes were checked; both alias entries are absent from observed_inputs. Confidence: high.

`refuse` publishes the refusal set to the caller's requested `--output-dir` path and re-resolves its parent at that moment. `Custody` captured and canonicalized the destination earlier. When `custody.verify()` fails because the destination parent changed (for example a symlink retargeted mid-run), the refusal set is written into the new, unvetted parent. That bypasses the parent-identity guard the drift check exists to enforce. Fix: when custody exists, publish refusals to `custody.destination()` (the captured canonical path). Skip publishing when the parent identity has drifted. ```rust // pass the canonical destination captured by Custody into refuse() // and do not re-resolve the requested path on a parent-drift refusal ``` *Spotted by [Graphite](https://app.graphite.com/diamond/?org=EffortlessMetrics&ref=ai-review-comment)*
